title: Closing an assessment triggers TrustScoreService.recalculate as a fire-and-forget side effect
description: AssessmentService.transition, when targetState === 'closed', calls `void trustScoreService.recalculate(organizationId, doc.vendorId.toString(), userId).catch(...)` — the transition response returns before recalculation necessarily completes, so this integration point must be tested for eventual consistency, not synchronous completion.
preconditions: An assessment in under_review with all responses accepted, for a vendor with an existing trust score document
steps: Call the transition endpoint to close the assessment
Poll GET /trust-score/:vendorId until lastRecalculatedAt updates or a timeout elapses
expectedResult: lastRecalculatedAt on the vendor's trust score document advances to a timestamp after the transition call, and a new trust-score-history entry with snapshotReason='recalculation' and triggeredBy=userId is written — confirming the fire-and-forget call actually executes rather than being silently dropped by an unhandled rejection.

title: vendor_assessment_closed and vendor_trust_score_recalculated PCL events are emitted with the correct organizationId/vendorId payload
description: eventBridgeService.emit() is called from both AssessmentService.transition (on close) and TrustScoreService.recalculate. These events feed the Project Compliance Lookup (PCL) pipeline that other modules (dashboard, GRC framework) read from — a malformed or missing event silently breaks cross-module analytics without an obvious error.
preconditions: Event bridge test harness capturing emitted events
steps: Close an assessment and capture the eventBridgeService.emit call
Independently trigger a trust score recalculation and capture its emit call
expectedResult: Two distinct events are captured: { eventType: 'vendor_assessment_closed', organizationId, vendorId, occurredAt } and { eventType: 'vendor_trust_score_recalculated', organizationId, vendorId, metadata: { overallScore, riskLevel }, occurredAt } — both with the correct, matching organizationId and vendorId for the test fixtures (not swapped or stale from a prior test run).

title: assertProjectAccess correctly calls out to vibrantix-backend's project-scope endpoint and honors both allow and deny responses
description: project-scope.ts's projectScopeClient.getScope(userId, organizationId) is an HTTP call to vibrantix-backend. This integration test verifies the real contract (not a mock): a project admin gets isProjectAdmin=true (bypasses filtering), a project member gets their projectIds populated, and a non-member gets a scope that does NOT include the target project.
preconditions: vibrantix-backend project-scope endpoint reachable in the test environment
Three seeded users: a project admin, a project member of project X, and a user who is a member of project Y only
steps: As the project X member, call assertProjectAccess for project X — expect no throw
As the project Y-only user, call assertProjectAccess for project X — expect AppError.forbidden
As the project admin, call assertProjectAccess for project X — expect no throw regardless of explicit membership
expectedResult: Each call resolves exactly as described — no cross-project data leaks and admin bypass works only for genuinely admin-scoped users, matching vibrantix-backend's resolveProjectScope contract.

title: Replacing vendor requirement mappings fires vendor_requirement_mapping_changed to sync compliance-frameworks coverage
description: PUT /evidence/:id/requirement-mappings diffs old vs new requirementCodes/UCL control ids and, only when there's an actual change, calls firePclEvent('vendor_requirement_mapping_changed', orgId, { vendorId, projectId, addedRequirementCodes, removedRequirementCodes, addedRequirementUcls, removedRequirementUcls }) against vibrantix-backend's /api/internal/pcl/events.
preconditions: An evidence document currently mapped to framework requirement codes ['A.5.19', 'A.5.20']
steps: Call PUT /evidence/:id/requirement-mappings replacing the mapping with ['A.5.19', 'A.5.22'] (drop A.5.20, add A.5.22)
Inspect the PCL event fired to vibrantix-backend
expectedResult: The event payload's addedRequirementCodes contains 'A.5.22' and removedRequirementCodes contains 'A.5.20' — 'A.5.19' (unchanged) appears in neither list, confirming the diff logic only reports the actual delta rather than the full new/old sets.

title: Approving a Trust Network access request creates an auto-reciprocal pending request on the requester's own config
description: TrustNetworkService.respondToRequest, on approval, fire-and-forgets a check of the requester's own trust network config: if the requester has sharingEnabled and is not already a partner/pending with the approver, it creates a reciprocal AccessRequest with requestReason:'auto-reciprocal' on the REQUESTER's config so the approving org can request access back.
preconditions: Org B has sent a pending access request to Org A
Org B's own trust network config has sharingEnabled = true and no existing relationship with Org A
steps: As Org A, approve Org B's pending access request
Fetch Org B's own trust network config's pendingRequests
expectedResult: Org B's config now contains a new pendingRequests entry with requestingOrgId = Org A's id, requestedBy='system', requestReason='auto-reciprocal', status='pending' — created automatically without any explicit action from Org A beyond the original approval.
